name: Persian alphabet
signature: Right-to-left joined letters on a flowing baseline; most short vowels are understood rather than printed.
combination: Most letters join and change shape by position. Alif ا and vav و do not connect to the following letter. Short vowels are normally omitted. Persian adds پ چ ژ گ to the Arabic inventory as the course expands.
notes: Starter inventory for the first Persian shared-spine lessons. Contextual shapes and stroke descriptions follow common Naskh handwriting; the course will grow toward the full Persian alphabet.

strokeOrder: draw the tall stem downward in one unbroken movement

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, opening ا demonstration at 00:08–00:11 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ا as one top-to-bottom Naskh stroke while presenting the alphabet right-to-left. Contextual joins change neighbouring ink, but the isolated non-connector remains the same one-stroke stem; this path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

letters.notes: Does not join to the following letter.

strokeOrder: sweep the shallow bowl from right to left
lift, then place the dot below

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, opening ب demonstration at 00:11–00:15 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ب as a shallow right-to-left Naskh bowl, followed by one pen lift and the separate dot below. Contextual joins reshape the bowl in connected text; this isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: sweep the shallow bowl from right to left
lift, then place the left dot below
lift again and place the right dot below
lift again and place the lower-center dot

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, پ demonstration at 00:16–00:21 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated پ as a shallow right-to-left Naskh bowl, followed by three separate dots below in left, right, then lower-center order. Contextual joins reshape the bowl in connected text; this isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: sweep the shallow bowl from right to left
lift, then place the left dot above
lift again and place the right dot

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, ت demonstration at 00:22–00:27 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ت as a shallow right-to-left Naskh bowl, followed by one lift to the left dot above and another lift to the right dot. Contextual joins reshape the bowl; this isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: draw the short upper head from left to right
continue down and around the deep bowl without lifting
lift once, then place the dot above

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, خ demonstration at 00:49–00:54 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated خ body-first: the short upper head travels left to right, then the same pen-down run turns through the hooked descent and deep bowl. After completing the body, the writer lifts once and places the single dot above. Contextual joins reshape the head; this isolated Persian learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline and retains Persian-scoped provenance rather than borrowing the separate Arabic or Urdu خ sources.

strokeOrder: begin at the upper tip and descend through the folded shoulder
without lifting, turn left along the baseline

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, د demonstration at 01:04–01:06 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated د as one continuous Naskh motion: it begins at the upper tip, folds through the shoulder, and turns left along the baseline without lifting. This non-connector does not join to a following letter; the learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline and records Persian-scoped provenance rather than borrowing the separate Arabic or Urdu د sources.

letters.notes: Does not join to the following letter.

strokeOrder: begin at the upper tip and descend through the short stroke
without lifting, sweep left through the lower curve

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, ر demonstration at 01:10–01:12 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ر as one continuous Naskh motion: it begins at the upper tip, descends through the short stroke, and sweeps left through the lower curve without lifting. This non-connector does not join to a following letter; the learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline and records Persian-scoped provenance rather than borrowing the separate Arabic or Urdu ر sources for the same Unicode glyph.

letters.notes: Does not join to the following letter.

strokeOrder: form the three teeth from right to left
flow into the final bowl without lifting

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, س demonstration at 01:29–01:35 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated س as one continuous right-to-left Naskh movement: three teeth flow directly into the final bowl with no pen lift. Contextual joins shorten the final bowl before following letters; this isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: draw the upright downward
turn into the base curve without lifting

strokeOrderSource.variation: The source shows isolated ل as one continuous Naskh stroke: the upright descends into the base curve with no pen lift. This path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: shape the round head
continue down the tail without lifting

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, م demonstration at 02:33–02:36 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The source shows isolated م as one continuous Naskh stroke: its round head flows into the descending tail with no pen lift. This path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: sweep the bowl from right to left
lift, then place the dot above

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, ن demonstration at 02:37–02:43 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The source shows isolated ن as one continuous right-to-left Naskh bowl, followed by one lift to place the dot above. Contextual joins reshape the bowl; this isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.

strokeOrder: loop the isolated body and finish left without lifting

strokeOrderSource.citation: Persian Online, How to Write Persian Characters, ه demonstration at 02:47–02:50 (Liberal Arts Instructional Technology Services, Univ. of Texas at Austin)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated ه as one simple closed handwritten loop with no pen lift. The vendored Noto Naskh isolated form is wider and has two counters plus a leftward baseline finish, so this learner path preserves the source's single pen-down run while fitting that typographic outline. Contextual joins use visibly different forms.

letters.notes: A final he can help write the vowel e.

strokeOrder: shape the small head loop
flow into the leftward tail without lifting

strokeOrderSource.variation: The cited freehand lesson demonstrates isolated و as one continuous Naskh stroke: its small head loops before flowing into the leftward curving tail with no pen lift. This non-connector does not join to a following letter; the isolated learner path fits the vendored Noto Naskh outline.
